The most serious crime he can be convicted of is **involuntary manslaughter**. Under transferred intent, his intent to commit a battery on the opposing player carries over to the teammate he killed, but intending only a slight wound does not supply the malice aforethought that murder requires. He could be charged with second-degree murder only if his jurisdiction treats the underlying shooting as an inherently dangerous felony for felony-murder purposes, which varies by state.

CONFIDENCE: 60
